failures.criterion: The GitHub intake processes notifications in order per pull request where order matters (acceptance 2; PR body: 'in order per pull request and per run')
failures.evidence: Real surface: two head binaries on one database and one NATS, fake GitHub holding each pulls/<n> GET 3 s; published PR 201 x3, 202-205 through the listener (`pub.sh 0 notifications.github.loadorg.loadrepo.pr.<n>`), SIGTERM to the bound process 1 s later. Fake log: the stopping process GET pulls/201 12:46:27.759 -> 12:46:30.760, while the standby (bound 12:46:30.590) started GET pulls/201 at 12:46:30.598: two fetches of one pull request overlapped, so an older fetch can be written after a newer one (UpsertRun, store.go:570, has no regression guard, so a run's in_progress fetch can overwrite its completed row). Cause: intakeDelivery.stop Naks the messages queued behind a key before that key's in-flight handler returns, and receive Naks buffered messages the same way. Red test (commit e95f54eb): `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:25432/dispatch_test?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/dispatch/delivery/ -run TestAHandOverKeepsAPullRequestsMessagesInOrder -count=1` fails: events ["start 1" "start 1" "end 1"]. Checked fixable: Naking the queued messages after keys.wait() makes it pass with the rest of the package.

failures.criterion: Dispatch's shutdown fits its budget (cmd/dispatch/shutdown.go stopGrace = 30 s; the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds 35 s, infra/gcp/dispatch_kube.go) now that the intake waits for its handlers
failures.evidence: Real surface, fake GitHub holding pulls/<n> 50 s: published PR 401, SIGTERM 2 s later; the head process exited 58.0 s after the signal (log: 'shutting down' 13:06:48.746, the handler's 'context deadline exceeded' 13:07:46.712, after three GitHub attempts). The base build c3d09eec924c under the same test (PR 402 held) exited 0.4 s after SIGTERM. In production the kubelet kills the process at 30 s, so every deploy during a slow GitHub ends with SIGKILL and the deferred closes after stopIntakes never run. Red test (commit e95f54eb): `go test ./internal/dispatch/delivery/ -run TestAStoppingIntakeDoesNotWaitOutAGitHubCallThatDoesNotAnswer -count=1` fails: still waiting 20 s after its context ended. Checked: the three tests (this one, the hand-over test and the existing TestAMessageQueuedBehindItsKeyAtStopIsRedeliveredAtOnce) can all pass with a bounded wait for in-flight handlers, then cancelling them, then Naking what was queued; cancelling at once alone breaks the existing test.

proof.surface: The head envoy-dispatch binary's intake, fed through the Envoy listener's POST /v1/messages/publish, against a fake GitHub holding each pulls/<n> GET 3 s

proof.criterion: A delivery settings change reaches the intake at once, and a freshness write does not reload it
proof.surface: PUT /api/v1/settings/delivery on the head binary, then a published PR merge
proof.command: api.sh 18778 PUT /api/v1/settings/delivery (population_authors + newbot), then pub.sh for PR 301 by newbot and PR 302 by stranger; psql updates of last_reconcile_at and excluded_repos

proof.negativeControl: update delivery_settings set last_reconcile_at = now() -> no settings read in the next 3 s.
